title: Customer readiness scorecard & escalation playbook for Hosted API streaming + toolchains
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background: We receive a steady stream of enterprise feature requests that combine streaming chat, multi-tool/function calling, and structured-output requirements. Current intake is manual and inconsistent: SEs and Solutions engineers triage via Slack and spreadsheets, which leads to uneven SLAs, missed preflight requirements (data residency, throughput commitments), and surprises during onboarding.

Problem statement: Enterprise customers often require deterministic performance and clear fallback behavior. Without a repeatable readiness assessment and a documented escalation path, onboards slip, support load increases, and teams make implicit trade-offs (e.g., accepting degraded latency) without engineering sign-off.

Goal: Create a lightweight automated "Customer Readiness Scorecard" plus an escalation playbook that: 1) produces an objective readiness score for Hosted API requests involving streaming + toolchains, 2) surfaces required non-functional constraints (SLA, residency, PII handling, throughput), 3) recommends one of three onboarding lanes (Self-serve, SE-assisted, Enterprise Concierge) and 4) defines clear escalation steps to Dedicated/Private or runtime changes when score falls below thresholds.

Scope: This ticket covers the product decision, scoring rubric, integration points (Console intake form, SE intake sheet, existing intake webhook), and playbook for Solutions/Support. It includes a first-pass UI wireframe for the Console intake page and a minimal automation that produces a PDF scorecard attached to the intake ticket.

Non-goals: Implementation of Dedicated or Private provisioning automation, deep UI polish, audit log retention policy changes (these will be follow-ups when lane decisions require provisioning).
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard schema defined with at least 8 signals: SLA latency, SLA availability, data residency, PII classification, average tokens per session, peak concurrent streams, toolchain complexity (number of external tools), structured-output strictness (schema enforcement)
Thresholds and lane recommendations documented (Self-serve: score >= 80; SE-assisted: 50-79; Enterprise Concierge: <50) and agreed with CS and Solutions
Console intake prototype mock uploaded and linked in 'links' with copy for each field and tooltip guidance
Escalation playbook with step-by-step actions for SE and Eng onboarding included: grooming checklist, required attachments (privacy review, load test plan), and owner handoff template
Automation design doc for generating a PDF scorecard attached to intake tickets, with webhook sample payload and example mapping to Redwood Console fields
